correctness.rationale: Christandl equation (15) verifies the normalization J_n=lambda sqrt(n(N-n))/2 and amplitude [-i sin(lambda t/2)]^(N-1). At t0+Xi, occupation probability is cos^(2m)(lambda Xi/2). Expanding the 2m-th cosine power gives the central binomial Fourier coefficients; the Gaussian characteristic function multiplies coefficient k by exp(-k^2 s^2/2), establishing the exact sum for all m>=1 and s>=0. Positive coefficients imply strict decrease for s>0, with endpoints 1 and 4^-m binom(2m,m). For s=c/sqrt(m), the pointwise log-cosine limit is -c^2 Z^2/4, with bounded integrand; dominated convergence gives (1+c^2/2)^-1/2. For fixed s>0, each central-binomial coefficient ratio tends to one and is bounded by one; the summable Gaussian weights and central-binomial asymptotic give the theta-series constant. Targets eta in (0,1) have a unique finite root only when eta exceeds the plateau; this holds eventually in m. Bracketing the strictly monotone limiting profile gives the stated target threshold without assuming unwarranted uniform convergence. Independent direct Gaussian integration agrees with the finite sum to about 2e-16 at four (m,s) pairs; this is supplemental numerical evidence, not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Gaussian full-line or wrapped timing model only; not worst-case errors, truncated readout distributions or arbitrary-state channel fidelity. No uploaded verifier was executed.

value.rationale: Timing precision is explicitly motivated in both the older review and the 2025 stochastic receiver framework. The exact finite-chain occupation law converts a Gaussian standard-deviation specification into a performance quantity. Its shrinking-noise profile gives a target-dependent calibration constant, whereas fixed noise retains periodic-revival contributions through a theta series. Distinguishing these regimes provides information beyond a local curvature or deterministic window and is a natural useful exact fact of an established chain, not an arbitrary finite slice.
residual_risks: The clock model is idealized and later transfer periods must count as equivalent; physical truncation or correlated clock effects require a different law.
